title: Moses says “send someone else” — Exodus 4
paragraphs: Moses says “send someone else” — Exodus 4
He had a burning bush in front of him.

And still said, “Lord… send someone else.”
(Exodus 4)

Moses was not refusing because God was unclear.
He was refusing because obedience felt heavier than hiding.
That’s the part that hits.

Some of us are not waiting for more confirmation.
We are just scared that calling will cost too much.

Moses had excuses.
“I’m not enough.”
“I’m not ready.”
“I can’t speak.”
And finally the real one comes out: “Please send someone else.”
Exodus 4:13
But here’s what we miss…

God did not choose Moses because Moses was fearless.
God chose Moses because God is enough for fearful men.

The miracle was never Moses’ confidence.
The miracle was God’s presence.
“I will be with you.”
That was the answer.
Not a polished résumé.
Not perfect eloquence.
Presence.
And maybe that is where this word finds you.

You keep asking God for another sign, another season, another version of yourself.
But the Lord is not looking for your strength before He sends you.
He is commanding your surrender because He goes with you.

Yes, Moses hesitated.
Yes, Moses trembled.
Yes, Moses argued.
But God still pursued him with mercy and holy fire.
And that points us to Jesus.

Because all of us, in one way or another, have said, “Send someone else.”
Someone else can forgive.
Someone else can obey.
Someone else can carry the cross.
But Jesus did not say that.

He came.
He obeyed.
He suffered.
He died for our rebellion, our excuses, our fear, our running.
And He rose again so that broken, hesitant people could be forgiven, restored, and sent in grace.

So this is the word:
Stop worshiping your weakness.
Start trusting your Savior.

The God who called Moses is still calling people who shake.
And the Christ who saves is still enough for people who stall.

Repent of delay.
Lay down the excuse.
Answer the voice of God.

Because “send someone else” may sound humble—
but sometimes it is fear dressed up as surrender.

Jesus is better than your fear.
And His grace is stronger than your no.
